name: TLV7021DBVR
title: Single and dual low-power 1.6 V to 6.5 V comparators, rail-to-rail inputs, push-pull or open-drain output (TLV7011, TLV7021, TLV7012, TLV7022)
summary: A family of micropower comparators drawing about 5 µA per channel with a typical propagation delay of 260 ns. They run from 1.6 V, accept inputs from VEE to 100 mV above VCC without output inversion, and have hysteresis built in. TLV7011 (single) and TLV7012 (dual) have push-pull outputs; TLV7021 (single) and TLV7022 (dual) have open-drain outputs that may be pulled above VCC. TLV7021DBVR is the open-drain single in a 5-pin SOT-23.

circuits.title: TLV701x inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: The input drives IN-, and IN+ sits at VA, set by a three-resistor network: R1 from the 5 V supply, R2 to ground and R3 back from the output. With the output high R3 is in parallel with R1, which raises VA to the upper threshold VA1; with the output low R3 parallels R2 and VA drops to VA2. With all three at 1 MΩ the output falls as the input passes 3.33 V and rises again once it drops below 1.67 V.
notes: The thresholds take the output high level as equal to VCC.

circuits.title: TLV701x noninverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: IN- is held at a 2.5 V reference. The input reaches IN+ through R1 (330 kΩ), and R2 (1 MΩ) feeds the output back to the same node. The output goes high once the input climbs to VIN1 and low again when it falls to VIN2; with a 5 V supply these are 3.325 V and 1.675 V, a window of VCC × R1 / R2.

circuits.title: Window comparator
circuits.description: Two TLV7021 open-drain comparators share one pull-up, RPU, to 3.3 V, so either one can pull the active-low UV_OV line to the microcontroller down. A string of three equal 10 MΩ resistors across the 3.3 V supply gives 2.2 V at the R1-R2 junction and 1.1 V at the R2-R3 junction. The sensor drives IN- of the upper comparator, whose IN+ is at 2.2 V, and IN+ of the lower one, whose IN- is at 1.1 V. UV_OV is high while the sensor sits between 1.1 V and 2.2 V and low outside that band; the large resistor values keep the divider current small.
notes: VCC is 3.3 V and VEE is ground for both comparators.
With R1 = R2 = R3, VTH+ is two thirds and VTH- one third of the 3.3 V supply.

circuits.title: IR receiver analog front end using TLV7011
circuits.description: A reverse-biased IR LED serves as the light detector, and R1 (10 MΩ) turns its photocurrent into a voltage at IN-, about 1 V for 100 nA. R2 and C1 (470 kΩ, 10 nF, roughly 4.7 ms) average that signal into Vref, which follows slow changes in received light but not the data bits. Vref reaches IN+ through R3, and R4 (10 MΩ) from the output adds hysteresis so the output does not chatter. The output goes to a microcontroller and can also wake it. The circuit runs from a 3 V coin cell, and the time constant is picked for data at 9600 baud.

parts.note: Reverse biased; used as the receiver.

parts.value: Output to MCU (also to wake-up MCU)

notes: U1 takes its supply from the 3 V cell (VCC) and ground (VEE).
Short, infrequent transmissions keep the drain on the coin cell low.

circuits.title: Square-wave oscillator
circuits.description: A relaxation oscillator. R1, R2 and R3 set VA on IN+ from V+, ground and the output, so the threshold moves between VA1 and VA2 as the output switches. C1 on IN- charges through R4 from the output until VC reaches VA1, the output drops, and C1 then discharges through R4 to VA2, when the output goes high again. With R1 = R2 = R3 the thresholds are 2/3 and 1/3 of the supply and the frequency is 1 / (2 R4 C1 ln 2).
notes: Values for the output waveform curve: all resistors 100 kΩ, C1 = 100 pF, V+ = 5 V and V– at ground, a 20 pF output load and 10 pF stray capacitance from VA to ground.
The highest usable frequency is limited by the propagation delay and the output load capacitance; the picoamp bias current lets a small C1 and a large R4 be used.

operation.text: TLV7011 and TLV7021 are single comparators; TLV7012 and TLV7022 are duals. The first of each pair (TLV701x) has a push-pull output that both sources and sinks milliamps, enough for an LED or a capacitive load, and needs no pull-up. The second (TLV702x) has an open-drain output that can be pulled up above VCC, which suits level shifting, wired-OR outputs and bipolar-to-single-ended conversion. Singles come in X2SON (0.8 mm × 0.8 mm), SC70 and SOT-23; duals in VSSOP, SOT-23-THIN and WSON. TLV7021DBVR is the open-drain single in SOT-23 on a 3000-piece reel, marked 1ID2.

The common-mode range runs from VEE to 100 mV above VCC, and any differential voltage within that range is allowed. Driving an input past either rail does not invert the output. The inputs tolerate up to 5.5 V whatever VCC is, including with VCC unpowered, and keep their high impedance, so inputs between 0 V and 5.5 V can be present while the supply ramps and no series resistor is needed. Bias current is about 1 pA between the rails. Below VEE, internal diodes to VEE conduct and the bias current climbs exponentially; it roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise.

The switching characteristic is set by the threshold, the input offset and the built-in hysteresis, a window about the offset-shifted threshold that keeps noise from toggling the output (4.2 mV typical on TLV7011). More hysteresis is added with external positive feedback.

A power-on-reset circuit is active while the supply ramps up or down. During that time a TLV701x holds its output low at VEE and a TLV702x leaves its output high impedance, a logic high. Once the supply is at or above the minimum operating voltage, the output follows the differential input; tON, 20 µs typical, is the time the supply must be above 1.6 V first.
The TLV701x push-pull stage draws no shoot-through current, which helps a tight power budget.

VS = VCC – VEE runs from 1.6 V to 5.5 V for the singles and to 6.5 V for the duals, from one supply or a split pair: 5 V and 0 V or ±2.5 V both give VS = 5 V. With split supplies the output low level is VEE. Capacitive load on the output and a high toggle rate raise the average supply current above the quiescent figure.

A 4 mil via from the X2SON centre pad to a bottom-layer ground trace or plane lowers board cost and improves reliability. A 100 nF capacitor across the supply pins is called for with a high-impedance or long supply path or a noisy supply, and when the output drives a long trace or a capacitive load: the fast edges and strong sink and source stages of TLV7011 and TLV7021 can pull supply current well above quiescent. A layout for the X2SON puts a 0.1 µF capacitor at the VCC pin, reached from the centre pad through a 4 mil via, a bottom-layer trace and an 8 mil via.

VCC is 3.3 V and VEE is ground. R1, R2 and R3 are 10 MΩ each, which puts the thresholds at 2.2 V and 1.1 V and keeps the divider current low. Open-drain TLV7021 outputs are used so the two can be tied together.

R1 must be large enough to give a usable signal at IN-, which the picoamp bias current allows; 10 MΩ gives 1 V per 100 nA. The R2-C1 time constant must suit the data rate, for example 9600 baud, so that Vref stays a valid threshold. R3 and R4 add hysteresis to stop false output transitions. The low quiescent and bias currents let the circuit run from a coin cell for years.

The period is set by R4 and C1. The top frequency is bounded by the propagation delay and the capacitance on the output. Because the bias current is tiny, a smaller capacitor with a larger resistor gives the same frequency, which saves cost and board area.
